faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full‑time role of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross pay. faqs.q: Does the casual loading apply to cloud engineer salaries?

If you are a casual employee not covered by an award, you are entitled to the 25% loading on top of the base rate. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains when it applies.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for a cloud engineer?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Cloud Engineer Salary

If you are a cloud engineer in Australia, you likely receive an hourly rate or an annual salary offer. Converting between the two helps you compare jobs, budget, and plan for tax and super. This guide explains how to convert your **cloud engineer salary** from hourly to annual using the standard 38‑hour week, and what to expect for casual loading, superannuation, and tax.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

For a full‑time cloud engineer working 38 hours per week, the calculation is straightforward. For example, if your hourly rate is $60:

$60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560 per year.

This is your gross annual salary before tax and before super (which is paid on top). The same formula works for any hourly rate. Use our [the timesheet](/) to enter your base rate and see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures instantly.

### Why 38 Hours?

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage based on a 38‑hour week. From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 ordinary hours. Most full‑time awards and agreements also use 38 hours as the standard. If your cloud engineer role specifies a different number of hours (e.g., 40 hours), substitute that number in the formula.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a $60‑per‑hour cloud engineer:

- Weekly: $60 × 38 = $2,280
- Fortnightly: $2,280 × 2 = $4,560

Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and aligning with pay cycles.

### Casual Loading and Super on Top

Two important additions can affect your total compensation:

**Casual loading:** Casual employees who are award‑free are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate under the National Minimum Wage Order. For a cloud engineer on $60 per hour, the casual rate would be $75 per hour ($60 × 1.25). However, many cloud engineers are permanent employees or covered by enterprise agreements that set a higher base rate without loading. Always check your employment type and award coverage. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page has more details.

**Superannuation:** From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For a $60‑per‑hour cloud engineer, that is an extra $7.20 per hour, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay—it is an additional contribution to your super fund. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for how salary sacrifice can affect this.

### Award Rates vs. Market Rates

Cloud engineer salaries are typically well above the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for awards such as the Professional Employees Award, which may cover some IT roles. However, most cloud engineers are employed under enterprise agreements or individual contracts that offer higher rates. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full‑time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026), which equates to about $54.83 per hour. Cloud engineers often earn more, reflecting specialised skills.

### Tax on Your Cloud Engineer Salary

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your take‑home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (generally). For a cloud engineer earning $118,560 per year, the tax estimate would be:

- Tax on $18,200: $0
- Tax on $26,800 (15%): $4,020
- Tax on $73,560 (30%): $22,068
- Total tax: $26,088
- Medicare levy (2% of $118,560): $2,371.20
- Total tax + Medicare: $28,459.20
- Estimated take‑home: $90,100.80 per year

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed calculation that includes the tax‑free threshold and Medicare.

### Comparing Job Offers

When comparing a cloud engineer salary offer, consider:

- Base hourly rate vs. annual salary
- Casual loading if applicable
- Superannuation (12% on top)
- Penalty rates, allowances, and overtime (not included in this basic conversion)
- Salary packaging options

Our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page helps you evaluate total remuneration.

### Important Notes

This conversion assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For award‑specific rates, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides and the Fair Work Commission’s National Minimum Wage Order. Our [reference tables](/data) provide historical data and comparisons.

### Start Your Calculation

Enter your base hourly rate on [the timesheet](/) to see your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember to check the casual loading box only if you are a casual employee receiving the 25% loading on top of your base rate—never enter a rate that already includes loading.
